title: Soils
standard_text: Describe the components of soil; compare sandy, clay and loam soils and how well they hold water; describe the role of living things such as worms and decomposers in soil. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand E: Earth and Space Systems – Soils in the Environment)
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets on what soil is made of, sandy, clay and loam soils, drainage and living things in soil. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Soil is a mixture of rock, humus, air and water.
key_sub: Sand drains fast, clay holds water, and loam is best for most plants.
body_html:
How to think about it

Soil is a mixture of tiny bits of rock, humus, air, water and living things.

  • Sandy soil drains fast; clay soil holds water and is sticky; loam is a good mix.
  • Humus comes from decaying plants and animals and adds nutrients.
  • Worms, insects, fungi and bacteria live in soil and keep it healthy.
Example

Which soil drains fastest?

big spaces between grains

Answer: sandy soil

Example

How do worms help soil?

tunnels

mixing

Answer: they let in air and water

Common mistakes

  • Thinking soil is just dirt with nothing living in it.
  • Thinking all soils are the same.
  • Thinking worms harm gardens.
